https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm3w.text: Figure caption, Watch: Timelapse shows typhoon barrelling towards Japan By Jamie Whitehead Â and Â Kurumi Mori ,Â Tokyo correspondent Published 21 September 2026 Updated 22 September 2026 06:58 BST Four people have died in Japan after Typhoon Dujuan battered Tokyo and surrounding prefectures with torrential rains and destructive winds, local reports said. The storm cut power for 50,000 people and caused the suspension of hundreds of flights. Most evacuation orders were lifted on Tueday as the storm pulled away from Japan's eastern coast. At the height of the storm on Monday, authorities warned of an "imminent threat to life" and urged 1.9 million people to move to shelters. The fatalities were from landslides in Kanagawa and Chiba prefectures. Six others were reported missing, public broadcaster NHK reported. Image source, EPA Image caption, Pedestrians caught in the rain at the Shibuya crossing in Tokyo Dujuan had sustained winds of 130km/h (81mph) and gusts of 194km/h. The typhoon is the latest in a series of storms in the Pacific, made more intense by the "super El NiÃ±o", which has warmed the ocean, fuelling the formation of storms. Authorities had advised the public to pay attention to weather information. Dujuan, which is Japan's 25th typhoon of the year, hit in the midst of a five-day holiday and forced the cancellation of several events. Concerts scheduled for Monday at the Rock in Japan music festival were cancelled, while the Tokyo Game Show, a video game convention, also cancelled Monday's programme. Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi offered her condolences in a post on X to those who lost their lives in the typhoon, before saying she would be continuing with her scheduled trip the United States as planned. "With a sense of urgency, I instructed Chief Cabinet Secretary Takehara and Minister Hosono to respond with utmost preparedness," she wrote, before saying she had boarded a flight to the US. She will be speaking at the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, and will meet with US President Donald Trump. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Passengers waiting for updates at Haneda Airport The Yokosuka City Fire Department told the BBC that a woman in Kanagawa prefecture, aged in her 60s, was believed to have been buried alive after a landslide swept the house she lived in. Following a search by rescue crews, she was found inside the home and pronounced dead, NHK reported. Separately, Sodegaura City Fire Department in Chiba prefecture told the BBC a man in his 50s was rescued after getting trapped while working to clear debris at a landslide site. The department said the worker fell into a bamboo thicket, along with some heavy machinery. He was then taken to hospital before his death was confirmed, according to local reports. Police are investigating the details of the incident. Image source, EPA Image caption, A woman struggles with her umbrella outside Shinjuku station Some research suggests that Japan has become more exposed to destructive storms, but climate change is not thought to be increasing the number of these storms globally, and could even make them less common in some regions. As temperatures rise, typhoons that do form are likely to become more intense on average, however. Warmer ocean waters mean storms can pick up more energy, leading to higher wind speeds. And because a warmer atmosphere can hold more moisture, these storms could also bring heavier rainfall. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Another woman also struggles with an umbrella in Chiba This year, El NiÃ±o - the natural weather phenomenon bringing warmer water to parts of the tropical Pacific - is another factor. El NiÃ±o doesn't have a clear effect on the total number of typhoons, but it can affect where typhoons form, their strength and which countries they hit. Some El NiÃ±o events may expose Japan to stronger typhoons, for example. The typhoon is continuing to travel along the country's Pacific coast, heading north. The extent of the damage today may not be known until Tuesday. Additional reporting by Chie Kobayashi and Mark Poynting, climate reporter Related topics Japan El NiÃ±o More on this story What is El NiÃ±o and why could it mean record temperatures? https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c607.text: Image source, Agencja Wyborcza.pl/Reuters Image caption, Polish police have sealed off the area around the abbey By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 1 hour ago A priest has been killed and four other people injured in a knife attack in south-east Poland, officials have said. A 31-year-old Ukrainian man was arrested after the stabbings on the grounds of a Catholic abbey in the town of JarosÅaw. Polish President Karol Nawrocki said Thursday's attack "has shaken us all and demands a firm response from the state", while his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky said "we are shocked by this evil". Reports in Polish media said the attacker first injured a priest in a nearby cafe, and then another four people inside the abbey itself. A police investigation into the attacker's motives is now under way. Polish police said four men and one woman were stabbed in the attack on Thursday morning on the abbey grounds. The name of the murdered priest has not been publicly released. Polish Interior Minister Marcin KierwiÅski said psychological support was now being provided to all those affected by the incident. Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the perpetrator "will be punished with the full severity of Polish law". Echoing his words, President Zelensky said "the perpetrator of this evil must bear full responsibility according to the law", adding that Ukraine was counting on "a quick and thorough investigation of all circumstances". The Ukrainian embassy in Poland also condemned the attack. In a statement, it said: "In such difficult moments, it is especially important to support each other, remain steadfast in respect for human life, and not allow pain to escalate into hatred or new violence. Responsibility for a crime must be based solely on the law." Poland has recently seen a number of often violent incidents involving its citizens and Ukrainians, many of whom have fled their home country after Russia's full-scale invasion. Skip next section Jammu and Kashmir Assembly passes resolution seeking urgent restoration of full statehood 09/28/2026 September 28, 2026 Jammu and Kashmir Assembly passes resolution seeking urgent restoration of full statehood Dharvi Vaid Dhulia The regional assembly of India-administered Kashmir on Monday passed a resolution seeking the urgent restoration of full statehood from its current status of a Union Territory, which is federally administered. The resolution was introduced by Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and was passed in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly amid chaos as legislators of the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) staged a walkout calling the non-binding resolution "unconstitutional" and "anti-national". The resolution calls on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government in New Delhi to ensure "the immediate and urgent restoration of full (federal) statehood to Jammu and Kashmir". In 2019, a contentious decision by the Modi government stripped Jammu and Kashmir of its semiautonomous status. The region was divided into two federally administered territories, bringing it directly under New Delhi's control. In 2024, the region elected its first government since being recategorized as a Union Territory with Abdullah's Jammu and Kashmir National Conference party at its helm. But the local government's powers are limited. The Modi government has consistently said that statehood for the territory would be granted at an "appropriate time". On Monday, Abdullah, who said that statehood was the territory's "right," sought a clarification on the timeline and questioned what "appropriate time" means, local Kashmir outlets reported. The text of Monday's resolution also referred to the constitutionally non-binding resolutions demanding federal autonomy, passed in 2000 and 2024. Modi's BJP, which is the largest opposition party in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly, strongly opposed the resolution with protests and sloganeering as Abdullah spoke ahead of the vote. BJP legislators also tore up copies of the resolution, reports said. Muslim-majority Kashmir has long been a bone of contention for India and Pakistan, both of whom lay claim to the restive, strategically important Himalayan region. https://p.dw.com/p/5NOwq Skip next section Chhattisgarh floods: Air Force personnel rescue 12 people stranded on hut roof 09/28/2026 September 28, 2026 Chhattisgarh floods: Air Force personnel rescue 12 people stranded on hut roof Dharvi Vaid Dhulia Heavy rains have wreaked havoc in the central Indian state of Chhattisgarh, causing rivers and streams to swell up and leading to flood-like conditions in some parts. Over 5,000 people were rescued over the weekend from the inundated areas and taken to relief camps and safer locations, according to reports. The districts of Bastar, Dhamtari, Bilaspur, Durg, Raipur, Balodabazar-Bhatapara and Narayanpur are among the regions affected by the heavy downpour. On Monday, the Indian Air Force (IAF) rescued 12 people stranded in a village on the northern bank of the Indravati river, which was flowing above the danger mark, news agency ANI quoted a Defense Ministry statement as saying. The group of people, which included women and children, were reportedly stuck on the roof of a hut which was at risk of collapsing due to the force of the floodwaters. An IAF commando was lowered on the roof from a helicopter, which hovered above as the people were pulled up, according to the ministry. How cities are fighting heat and floods To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video https://p.dw.com/p/5NOMm Skip next section India's Supreme Court takes note of recent Delhi-NCR rape cases 09/28/2026 September 28, 2026 India's Supreme Court takes note of recent Delhi-NCR rape cases Dharvi Vaid Dhulia The Supreme Court of India said on Monday that the recent slew of rape cases in the Indian capital of New Delhi and its neighboring districts "starkly underline a systematic failure" by law enforcement and public administrative authorities, legal news websites reported. The top court made the statement as it opened a "suo motu cognizance" legal review of the latest cases of rape in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR), LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. In Indian law, a suo motu cognizance refers to a court taking notice of a matter on its own initiative, without a formal petition or complaint being filed. The two-judge bench expressed its distress over the news reports of the recurring sexual violence and underpinned the need to fix accountability, LiveLaw reported. "These incidents considered alongside other recent reports of sexual offences across Delhi-NCR starkly underline a systematic failure on the part of the law enforcement and the public administrative authorities to guarantee basic public safety," LiveLaw quoted the bench as saying. Last week, Delhi saw hundreds of students protesting and expressing their outrage over the safety of women after a teenage girl was allegedly gang raped by three men at a public park in the capital. In August, media reports said that a ​17-year-old ‌girl was allegedly gang raped in a bus moving from Noida, a staellite city of the Indian capital, to Delhi by the vehicle's driver and conductor. The court on Monday said that public spaces, including parks, roads, buses, metro stations, subways and footbridges, cannot be allowed to become "high-risk zones" over inadequate illumination or surveillance, lack of patrolling, or other preventable administrative inadequacies, Bar and Bench reported. Supreme court says need to fix accountability The judges drew parallels with the 2012 fatal Delhi gang rape on a bus that came to be known as the Nirbhaya case. "One cannot help but draw painful parallels to the Nirbhaya incident of 2012," LiveLaw reported the bench as saying. The court also observed whether the systematic law enforcement apparatus has made any meaningful advancement since the Nirbhaya case, according to LiveLaw. The court stressed that "expressions of solidarity" were not a solution to the offences it called "social evil," adding that a "measurable response" was required with fixing "responsibility and accountability" upon the authorities entrusted with crime prevention, maintenance of public order and protection of vulnerable persons, according to local outlets. The private university located in the city of Phagwara witnessed massive student unrest after claims spread on social media that a female university student was allegedly raped within the campus premises by an outsider and had later died by suicide. The protests grew to be violent when the protesters clashed with the police, pelted stones at the security personnel, smashed windows and set fire to some objects within the university complex, reports said. Some students later claimed in social media posts that the vandals were not students, but outsiders. Heavy police deployment The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days, news agency ANI cited a statement from LPU as saying. The statement said students could travel to their hometowns during the suspension of classes and advised those who stay back to remain in their hostels or places of accommodation and avoid any unnecessary movement. The statement also called on students to avoid involvement in the unrest. Over 2,000 police personnel were deployed to ensure security on the campus, reports quoted the Additional Director General of Police Fayaz Farooqui as saying. The protesters also blocked the national highway between Jalandhar and Phagwara highway early Sunday, leading to traffic disruptions. On Monday, police said that the situation had been brought under control and traffic movement on the highway had been restored. Claims of rape remain unverified Meanwhile, the police are yet to confirm whether a student was raped within LPU's campus. They have launched an investigation to examine the facts of the incident. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has taken note of the situation and has directed the Director General of Police to visit the campus, reports said on Monday. Meanwhile, the Punjab State Women Commision is seeking a detailed report on the alleged rape, ANi reported. What has LPU said? The LPU has denied that the alleged rape took place, calling the claims "false, baseless and fabricated rumors". The university on Sunday posted a video with three female students who it said reside in the girls' hostel room where the alleged incident is claimed to have taken place. The video purportedly shows the girls denying that there had been a rape, with one of them asking the police to stop visiting the room repeatedly. However, media reports on Monday said that the same girls later appear in a separate purported video, claiming that they were instructed on what to say in the statement. https://stereogum.com/2514058/deafheaven.text: News Deafheaven Release New Surprise EP At Work In The Fields Of The Bomb TB By Tom Breihan 9:02 AM EDT on October 9, 2026 Add Stereogum to Google 10 Comments Last month, Deafheaven guitarist Kerry McCoy mentioned mysterious plans for a new EP. Talking to the Spanish website Binaural , McCoy said the new record would be both "the heaviest" and "the hardest" thing that the band had ever done — a big claim when this band is the one under discussion. He also said that it would be out "before the end of the year." Right now, Deafheaven are on tour with fellow heavy music titans Mastodon and Alcest, and we've been seeing reports about the band selling that new EP at the merch tables. Now, it has arrived. Deafheaven's new EP it's called At Work In The Fields Of The Bomb . Kerry McCoy was telling the truth about the record arriving before the end of 2026. It's a little early to say how it stacks up against the rest of the band's catalog in terms of both heaviness and hardness, but it is definitely both hard and heavy. On this one, the band follows the ferocious path of last year's spectacular Lonely People With Power . This time, they've got a very specific reason in mind. At Work In The Fields Of The Bomb is named after a photo book from Robert Del Tredici, which depicts the regular people involved in manufacturing nuclear weapons, one of those things that drives home the banality of evil in stark and tangible ways. The EP has three tracks in 23 minutes, and it ends with the absolutely overwhelming 13-minute epic "Sorry Laid The Hearth," which just seems to pick up intensity as it keeps going. I'm on my first listen right now, and this motherfucker will pulverize you. Deafheaven have been playing "Hunter" live since last week's Chicago show, which also seems to be when they started selling the At Work In The Fields Of The Bomb vinyl at the merch table. The song seems to sample the same Conet Project recording heard on Wilco’s “Poor Places.” Director Nico Poalillo's "Hunter" video was shot by Janusz Kamiński, the legendary Polish cinematographer who has been Steven Spielberg's guy for decades and who won Oscars for Schindler's List and Saving Private Ryan . That's awesome. Below, listen to At Work In The Fields Of The Bomb and check out Deafheaven's remaining tour dates.
